Question
========
A Quarto document has two R chunks. The first chunk creates an object called `x`. Can the second chunk use `x`,
without recreating it?

Answerlist
----------
* No, each chunk runs in its own isolated environment.
* Yes, because all R chunks in a document share a single, continuous session.
* Only if both chunks have the same label.
* Only if the `cache: TRUE` option is set on the first chunk.

Solution
========

Answerlist
----------
* Wrong: R chunks are not isolated from one another.
* Correct: chunks in the same language run in one shared session, so objects persist across chunks in the order they appear.
* Wrong: chunk labels identify chunks for referencing and error messages; they don't control whether objects are shared.
* Wrong: caching affects whether a chunk's computation is rerun on subsequent renders; it isn't required for objects to be shared within a single render.
